name: courtlistener-10pct
provenance: The larger sample published next to the one-percent file; eyecite's workflow does not use it. It was re-uploaded on 2025-07-28. 11 rows have every text column empty and go in as empty documents, as eyecite's benchmark would send them. eyecite's .github/workflows/benchmark.yml (v2.7.8) documents the query that made the ten-percent file: COPY (SELECT id, plain_text, html, html_lawbox, html_columbia, html_anon_2020, xml_harvard FROM search_opinion TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (0.1)) TO STDOUT WITH (FORMAT csv, ENCODING utf8, HEADER), bzip2-compressed. Postgres reads 0.1 as a percentage, so the one-percent and ten-percent names are labels for the two file sizes, not sampling rates.
